# Shape: rows are not the only axis

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask bench-shapes` from crates/engine/examples/bench_shapes.rs. Don't edit by hand. -->

> **Generated** for Cella 0.13.0 at `b6e4cfc` (2026-11-24). Machine: windows x86_64. The same commands at three workbook shapes, each with the same number of cells.

Every other ruler here varies **rows**. This one holds the cell count at 8,000,000 and moves them around: the same eight million cells as a million-row sheet, as a thousand-column sheet, and as a hundred sheets of ten thousand rows. A command that is O(columns) or O(sheets) has no way to show it in a row count, and a row-only ruler reports such a command as fast.

| shape | rows | columns | sheets | what it is |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `tall` | 1,000,000 | 8 | 1 | a million rows, eight columns |
| `wide` | 8,000 | 1,000 | 1 | a thousand columns, eight thousand rows |
| `sheets` | 10,000 | 8 | 100 | a hundred sheets of ten thousand rows |

A cell is the command's own wall clock, run alone in a fresh session holding a copy of that shape, with its region-naming params over the whole used area — the same generator the command catalogue uses.

Two things to read with care. **A command that works on one sheet sees only the active sheet's cells in the `sheets` shape** (10,000 × 8 = 80,000 of the eight million), so its `sheets` cell is a smaller job, not the same one; `file.saveBytes` and `sheet.rename` are the rows whose axis really is the sheet count. And **`home.formatCells` refuses a range over 4,000,000 cells** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`), so its two big shapes show that refusal instead of a number.

| command | what it does | tall | wide | sheets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `edit.find` | scans every used cell | 226 us | 71 us | 34 us |
| `edit.clearFormats` | walks every cell's style | 173 ms | 36 ms | 1.1 ms |
| `home.formatCells` | writes a style per cell | (params: selection too large to f…) | (params: selection too large to f…) | 17 ms |
| `edit.clearAll` | clears the used area | 9.2 ms | 1.1 ms | 3.1 ms |
| `data.sortAscending` | sorts the body by one column | 1.22 s | 2.04 s | 15 ms |
| `range.move` | moves a block | 1.35 s | 2.22 s | 22 ms |
| `home.autofitColumnWidth` | measures every column | 176 ms | 1.8 ms | 6.5 ms |
| `file.saveBytes` | serialises the workbook | 1.85 s | 1.46 s | 1.47 s |
| `home.conditionalFormat` | a conditional-format rule over the area | 851 us | 59 us | 198 us |
| `data.filter` | an AutoFilter over the area | 778 us | 41 us | 91 us |
| `edit.copy` | copies the area | 9.4 ms | 859 ms | 26 ms |
| `sheet.rename` | per-sheet work (should follow sheets, not cells) | 7.2 ms | 64 us | 7.9 ms |

## Where the shape changes the answer

Same cells, same command, a different arrangement — and more than four times apart. A row whose `sheets` cell is one percent of the cells (`data.sortAscending`, `edit.clearAll`, `edit.clearFormats`, `edit.find`) is a spread between the tall and wide columns, not across all three:

| command | fastest shape | slowest shape | times |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `edit.clearFormats` | sheets (1.1 ms) | tall (173 ms) | **162×** |
| `data.sortAscending` | sheets (15 ms) | wide (2.04 s) | **135×** |
| `sheet.rename` | wide (64 us) | sheets (7.9 ms) | **123×** |
| `range.move` | sheets (22 ms) | wide (2.22 s) | **99×** |
| `home.autofitColumnWidth` | wide (1.8 ms) | tall (176 ms) | **97×** |
| `edit.copy` | tall (9.4 ms) | wide (859 ms) | **91×** |
| `data.filter` | wide (41 us) | tall (778 us) | **19×** |
| `home.conditionalFormat` | wide (59 us) | tall (851 us) | **14×** |
| `edit.clearAll` | wide (1.1 ms) | tall (9.2 ms) | **9×** |
| `edit.find` | sheets (34 us) | tall (226 us) | **7×** |
